contracts.commit_point: pipeline._execute_sql_plan issues result = await db.execute(plan.sql, limit=..., timeout_seconds=...) (pipeline.py:387); the effect lands at the engine when _execute_cursor calls cursor.execute(rendered_sql) on the pooled read-only cursor (db.py:208-210).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Layered governed-SQL gate: (1) sqlgate.validate_select_sql parses with sqlglot (read='duckdb'), requires exactly one exp.Select, scans the AST for _FORBIDDEN node types and _DANGEROUS_TVFS function names, and enforces the live approved-table set built by build_live_schema (approved prefixes dim_/fact_/mart_/analytics_ plus ALLOWED_TABLES_FOR_AGENT); (2) sqlglot optimizer.optimize against the live schema catches unknown/ambiguous references; (3) catalog-scoped _detect_fan_chasm flags one_to_many joins with additive SUM lacking a collapsing GROUP BY. The gate is bound as a mandatory precondition in pipeline._prepare_sql_plan, invoked on the initial plan (pipeline.py:291) and again on repaired SQL (pipeline.py:364); gate failure yields _SqlPreparation.error with ChatError(_ERR_GATE_FAILED), preventing _execute_sql_plan from running. Complementary declared layer: the singleton connection is opened read_only=True so DuckDB itself refuses DDL/DML.
contracts.forbidden_condition: Agent-supplied SQL reaching DuckDB execution without passing the governed gate: SQL that is not exactly one SELECT statement, that contains any _FORBIDDEN AST node type (Attach/Copy/Create/Delete/Drop/Insert/Update/Merge/Alter/AlterColumn/Pragma/Set/SetItem/Command), that calls a _DANGEROUS_TVFS function, that references tables outside the approved warehouse set or uses catalog/schema-qualified references, that references no warehouse table, or that trips the one-to-many additive-SUM fan/chasm detector without a collapsing GROUP BY.

contracts.protected_operation: Execution of the agent-produced SQL string (plan.sql) against the process-wide read-only DuckDB connection via DuckDBSingleton.execute (reached through pipeline._execute_sql_plan).
contracts.protected_resource: The DuckDB analytics warehouse database opened read-only by DuckDBSingleton (duckdb.connect(db_path, read_only=True)); per the module docstring, multiple read-only processes share data/nba.duckdb and the engine refuses DDL/DML on read-only handles.
contracts.protection_obligation: Every agent-generated SQL statement (SqlPlan.sql, including post-repair SQL produced via repair_sql) must pass validate_governed_sql before it is executed against the read-only DuckDB warehouse: the gate accepts only a single read-only SELECT, rejects forbidden statements (Attach, Copy, Create, Delete, Drop, Insert, Update, Merge, Alter, AlterColumn, Pragma, Set, SetItem, Command), rejects dangerous table-valued functions (read_csv/read_parquet/read_ family and pragma_*/duckdb_* introspection TVFs), restricts table references to the approved live-schema allowlist, rejects catalog/schema-qualified references and FROM-less SELECTs, and applies live-schema optimizer checks plus catalog-scoped fan/chasm detection; a failed or unrepaired gate blocks execution and surfaces ChatError(_ERR_GATE_FAILED) instead of running db.execute. (Merged from both reviewer opinions, which describe the same gate-before-execution obligation.)
scope_limits: Contract covers only the chat-turn SQL path shown in supplied source (run_turn -> _stream_sql_plan -> _prepare_sql_plan/_execute_sql_plan); no claim is made about unseen entry points or callers.

Other db.execute / db.dry_run call sites in supplied source run operator-fixed SQL (build_live_schema information-schema introspection at sqlgate.py:182-186, check_connection SELECT 1 at db.py:459-476, dry_run EXPLAIN at db.py:357-372) and are not shown to be agent-mediated.
dry_run (EXPLAIN) touches plan/bind only and never row data; it is part of post-gate preparation, not an independently guarded commit.
Fan/chasm detection is deliberately conservative: it skips ambiguous alias cases and does not unravel CTEs/subqueries (sqlgate.py:405-443), so it is a partial, declared-only protection layer.
Row caps, the timeout watchdog, and memory_limit are runtime/cost controls (db.py:176-222, db.py:264-267), not part of this forbidden-condition contract.
